episodes.160933: An upper disturbance combined with a surface trough and daytime heating to produce scattered thunderstorms, an isolated one reached severe limits.
episodes.160938: Thunderstorms produced isolated gusty winds during the afternoon, with additional gusty winds in the evening and overnight.
episodes.160967: A slow moving cold front moved across a modestly unstable airmass in VT during the late afternoon/evening hours. Scattered thunderstorms developed along this line with a few storms producing some isolated strong winds and most storms very heavy rainfall.
episodes.161180: A broken line of showers and a few thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front that was approaching central Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening of September 8, 2021. One particular cell along this line intensified over Mifflin County and produced sporadic wind damage as it progressed eastward across Snyder and Northumberland counties. This cell also produced two weak tornadoes (an EF-0 and an EF-1) in Snyder County.
episodes.161292: An isolated strong to severe storm produced up to quarter sized hail.
episodes.161665: Light steering flow and sufficient low-level moisture combined with strong daytime heating and local effects to generate heavy showers and thunderstorms across most of interior Puerto Rico.
episodes.162055: Tropical Storm Mindy developed just southwest of the area and moved northeastward, bringing with it heavy rain and gusty winds with several reports of trees and power lines down and some flooding.  Two homes were damaged in Leon county from falling trees, but no injuries were reported.  One brief tornado occurred in a rural, forested area of Wakulla county with no structural damage.
episodes.162111: A tropical low was approaching the FL panhandle from the Gulf of Mexico with deep tropical moisture on the east side of the system overspreading the local forecast area under SSW flow. Showers and storms developed west to east through the day with storm enhancement toward the I-95 corridor and east coast where an east coast sea breeze drifted inland.
episodes.162288: A cold front moved into the mid-Atlantic late on September 8. Widespread showers and thunderstorms developed in a warm and humid air mass ahead of the front, moving into eastern Pennsylvania during the evening and early overnight hours. With instability waning after dark, much of the convection remained sub-severe. However, some instances of damaging wind did occur, particularly along a bowing line segment in Berks County. Showers and storms continued to gradually weaken as they shifted east later in the night.
episodes.162387: A cold frontal boundary moved southeast across the area during the afternoon of September 8th, 2021.  As the front moved southeast, an isolated supercell developed across Montgomery county, Kansas and produced quarter sized hail.
episodes.162414: An EF-1 tornado touched down Washington Township, Snyder County in the early evening of September 8, 2021. The tornado tracked southeastward for around three quarters of a mile, and had a maximum path width of around 30 yards.
episodes.162415: An EF-0 tornado touched down along Neitz Valley Road to the southeast of Freeburg during the early evening of September 8, 2021. The tornado tracked eastward for a little under 1.5 miles, and had a maximum path width of approximately 30 yards.
episodes.162458: Thunderstorms developing along a stationary front across north Georgia produced isolated  reports of wind damage in a portion of the metro Atlanta area. This front also triggered training storms that quickly dumped several inches of rain over the two-county area. Flash flooding occurred late in the evening on September 7th and continued into the early morning hours on September 8th. Afternoon showers and thunderstorms re-fired on the afternoon of September 8th with isolated flash flooding occurring again over-soggy north Fulton county.
episodes.162546: Numerous thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours within a tropical airmass ahead of newly formed Tropical Storm Mindy centered in the northeast Gulf of Mexico. A few storms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts.
episodes.162547: Numerous thunderstorms developed across southeast South Carolina in the afternoon hours within a tropical airmass ahead of newly formed Tropical Storm Mindy centered in the northeast Gulf of Mexico. A few storms moved to the coastline and adjacent coastal waters, producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.162658: Tropical Storm Mindy developed on the southwestern edge of the coastal waters and moved through the area, bringing tropical storm conditions.  Prior to its development, the area of disturbed weather brought squally conditions with occasional gusty winds.
episodes.162965: A well-organized line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed early afternoon on Tuesday, September 7th, along and ahead of an advancing cold front. The  majority of the damage was observed north of I-69 in cities such as Midland and Saginaw, where extensive tree damage, power outages, and 1 hail were observed; however, less widespread reports were received south of the I-69 corridor. The line of storms farther south was followed by a swath of high winds, where sustained winds (not associated with thunderstorms) were observed to be 40-50 mph, with gusts up to 60 mph. Between the severe thunderstorms and high winds, approximately 150,000 customers lost power.
episodes.162987: An isolated severe thunderstorm resulted in some wind damage to trees.
episodes.163041: A cluster of showers and storms producing heavy rain develop across Warren County in central North Carolina along a slow moving mid level disturbance in advance of a slow moving cold front. The heavy rain produced a couple of reports fo flash flooding across Warren County.
episodes.163057: A rapidly deepening surface low and its associated cold front moved across northwest Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening hours. Elevated thunderstorms developed behind the cold front and a few of the storms produced sporadic damaging winds with a few downed trees and minor structure damage primarily around Lake Nebagamon.
episodes.163104: A weak cold front pushed southward across north central Alabama during the afternoon on September 8th.  The air mass ahead of the front was moderately unstable with SBCAPE values near 4400 J/kg and DCAPE values near 1200 J/kg.
episodes.163160: A cold front moved into northern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 7th, helping to initiate thunderstorms. Several of the thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts and hail.
episodes.163180: Thunderstorms developed and moved west across southern Cochise County during the late afternoon and evening hours and produced large hail up to 2 inches in diameter from Douglas to the Bisbee and Sierra Vista areas.
episodes.163200: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in widespread damage over eastern New York on Wednesday September 8, 2021.
episodes.163360: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central and eastern Virginia.
episodes.163371: Numerous strong thunderstorms tracked through Lake St. Clair and the St. Clair and Detroit Rivers.
episodes.163396: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the Rappahannock River.
episodes.163397: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.163454: Cold advection behind Monday's thunderstorm line and cold frontal passage allowed for sufficient instability to develop over Lake Ontario for some early morning waterspouts. As the day ensued, shear increased, so while the waterspout threat diminished, the threat for gusty winds in showers increased, resulting in isolated convective wind gusts along the shoreline.
episodes.163506: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed throughout western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief large hail and gusty winds.

events.narrative: Quarter sized hail was reported.

The Fulton County Emergency Manager and local utility companies reported several trees and power lines blown down across the area from College Park to Alpharetta.

Numerous social media posts and reports from Emergency Management indicated significant flooding over Cobb county due to anomalously heavy rainfall. ||Radar estimates indicate 5 to 7 inches of rain accumulated quickly over the area resulting in the flash flooding. These amounts are between 0.1% and 0.2% chance of occurrence in a given year according to the NOAA Atlas 14.||In total, more than 250 structures, 15 roadways and more than 100 cars were inundated with floodwater. The Emergency Management reported flooding of the Roswell Road and Old Canton Road intersection, a washout of East Lake Parkway, a washed out footbridge near Chinquapin Drive and South Woodland Drive, and complete collapse and washout of Pickens Industrial Drive. ||Additionally, dozens of cars were flooded in the parking lot of the Marietta Crossing Apartment homes due to flash flooding of Rottenwood Creek. Water also caused damage to the interior of the building after water inundated the apartments.||Flash flooding occurred along Columns Drive along the western bank of the Chattahoochee River, inundating multiple homes and vehicles. This flooding was also documented by a local news station traffic helicopter on Twitter.||The river gage on Sope Creek (NWS MARG1/USGS 02335870) recorded an almost 17 foot rise in 4 hours due to the quickly accumulating rainfall. The observed stage height crest in Major Flood Stage at 18.05 feet -- only 0.3 feet below the crest from the historic September 2009 floods. Two river gages on the Chattahoochee River in Vinings (NWS VING1/USGS 02336000  and NWS VIXG1/USGS 02335990) also rose above flood stage.
The Cobb County Emergency Manager reported a few trees blown down in east Cobb County on Somerset Court and along Shadowlawn Road.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding over portions of north Fulton county due to quickly accumulating rainfall over the area.  Radar estimates indicate 3 to 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding. According to the NOAA Atlas 14, these rainfall amounts have a 0.5% to 0.2% chance of occurrence in a given year. ||The Emergency Manager reported flash flooding at the intersection of Willeo Road and Azalea Drive, Haynes Bridge Road and Westside Parkway, and Riverside Road along the Chattahoochee River. Flooding at Encore Parkway at North Point Center East caused at least one vehicle to stall in the intersection.

An EF-1 tornado touched down along Route 104 just north of Parkwoods Road in Washington Township, Snyder County in the early evening of September 8, 2021. The tornado tracked southeastward for around three quarters of a mile, produced estimated maximum winds of around 95 mph, and had a maximum path width of around 30 yards, before lifting near Redcort Lane. Upwards of 100 trees were knocked down in a forested area near Redcort Lane.
Quarter size hail was reported.

An EF0 tornado touched down along Neitz Valley Road near Bressler Lane, to the southeast of Freeburg, during the early evening of September 8, 2021. The tornado flattened part of a cornfield before tracking southeastward for a little under 1.5 miles. It produced estimated maximum winds of around 80 mph, and had a maximum path width of approximately 30 yards. As the tornado tracked eastward, it snapped and uprooted several trees along and just north of Neitz Valley Road and Produce Road. Trees were also uprooted in a heavily wooded area just north of Inch Hill Road before the tornado lifted.
